facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman with multiple sclerosis
treated with fingolimod for 3 years
tender nodule on her forehead, which had gradually grown over 3 weeks
bumping her forehead on an air-conditioning unit several months prior
denied fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia
Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
No other lesions on full-body skin examination
White blood cell count: 3.9/μL
Lymphocyte count: 0.65/μL
Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
Tissue culture: Grew Cryptococcus neoformans
HIV test: Negative

support_spans: Skin biopsy: Granulomatous inflammation composed of histiocytes, giant cells, and lymphocytes admixed with numerous narrow-budding yeasts with thick capsules
concepts.why: The presence of a fungal infection, as evidenced by the skin biopsy and tissue culture, supports this diagnosis.

support_spans: Eroded, crusted papule on the left forehead
concepts.why: The presence of a skin lesion could suggest sporotrichosis, but the tissue culture result rules out this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.why: The evidence of a specific skin lesion described as an eroded, crusted papule on the forehead, combined with the skin biopsy and tissue culture results, decided it.
